| Opponent | Our W / D / L (score rate) | Implied Elo |

| [Tianqi V1.1.8](iter2_vs_tianqi118_180pairs.compact.json) | 109/79/172 (41.25%) | ≈2,369 |
| [Cyclone 2007C](iter2_vs_cyclone2007c_180pairs.compact.json) | 60/95/205 (29.86%) | ≈2,452 |
| [Pikafish 2026-01-31 · UCI_Elo=1900](iter2_vs_pikafish_elo1900_180pairs.json) | 169/68/123 (56.39%) | ≈1,945 (limited-strength scale) |
| [Pikafish 2026-01-31 · full strength](iter2_vs_pikafish_official_180pairs.json) | 6/44/310 (7.78%) | ≈3,573 (cross-generation comparison) |

Conversion: `opponent reference Elo + 400 × log10(score / (1 − score))`. Reference ratings: [public Xiangqi engine rating list](https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/2072972857840350627): ElephantEye 2130.4, Tianqi 2430, Cyclone 2600, full-strength Pikafish 4002.7; Pikafish 1900 uses its built-in strength-limiting scale.

Three nearby historical engines imply **2369–2452 Elo**, centered around **2400 Elo**, at **human-master level on the cited scale**. The Pikafish rows compare limited and full strength of a modern engine.

All matches use 180 color-swapped opening pairs, 360 games, and fixed single-core affinity. Mean measured times (our engine / opponent): ElephantEye 104.0 / 119.4 ms, Tianqi 155.0 / 159.6 ms, Cyclone 112.4 / 89.9 ms, Pikafish 1900: 76.2 / 101.3 ms; full strength: 86.9 / 91.4 ms. Our engine used about 25% more time against Cyclone; the reported result retains that condition.

Reproduce with `run_eleeye_match.ps1`, `run_tianqi_match.ps1`, `run_cyclone_match.ps1`, and `run_external_match.ps1`. Per-game JSON records outcomes, openings, colors, search statistics, executable/model SHA-256 hashes, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals.
